questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Describe the mood or tone of an image when relevant
questions.stem: Wes's alt text describes objects but omits the tense, crowded mood of a tank photo, losing emotional context.

options.text: Screen readers cannot convey mood effectively.
Mood is subjective and never belongs in alt text.
Including mood or tone can convey emotional context when relevant.
Mood description is always more important than object description.

questions.explanation: Mood can add context when relevant. It should complement, not replace, object description.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use position to signal priority on a label
questions.stem: Xander places the least important field at the top of his label, burying the species name below.

options.text: Readers scan labels in random order.
Position does not affect which field readers see first.
Bottom placement is always better for primary information.
The most important field should occupy the top position.

questions.explanation: Top position signals priority. Placing important information low buries it.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use lighting to highlight wayfinding cues
questions.stem: Yara's wayfinding sign is in a dim corner, so visitors miss it; what lighting change would help?

answer.exemplar: Adding focused lighting to the sign would make it visible and draw visitors' attention in the dim corner.

questions.explanation: Poor lighting hides signs. Focused lighting draws attention and improves visibility.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use keyboard shortcuts for power users

stimulus.body: Zoe's tank app has no keyboard shortcuts, slowing down expert users who prefer quick navigation.

questions.stem: What would improve efficiency for Zoe's expert users?

options.text: Power users do not need shortcuts; they can click faster.
Keyboard shortcuts would speed navigation for power users.
Shortcuts clutter the interface and reduce usability.
Removing features simplifies navigation for everyone.

questions.explanation: Keyboard shortcuts speed expert navigation. Clicking or removing features are poor substitutes.
questions.hint: Add keyboard shortcuts for power users.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use consistent typeface across related documents
questions.stem: Amir uses different typefaces in his tank log and specimen labels, creating an inconsistent brand feel.

options.text: Readers do not notice typeface differences across documents.
Different typefaces per document add variety and interest.
Consistent typeface across documents would unify the visual identity.
Typeface consistency is only needed within a single page.

questions.explanation: Consistent typeface across documents unifies identity. Variety or single-page thinking undershoots.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use white space and colour together to signal inactive states
questions.stem: Bella's inactive buttons are bright blue, confusing users who try to click them.

options.text: Removing inactive buttons entirely avoids confusion.
Bright inactive buttons are fine because users learn quickly.
Inactive states do not need visual distinction.
Muting colour and adding grey would signal the inactive state clearly.

questions.explanation: Inactive states need muted colour. Bright colours mislead users into clicking.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Describe scale and size in image descriptions

stimulus.body: Carlos's alt text says 'a fish' without mentioning it is tiny compared to the tank, missing scale context.

questions.stem: What is missing from Carlos's alt text?

options.text: Scale is irrelevant to image understanding.
The scale or relative size of the subject.
Screen readers can infer scale from image dimensions.
Captions always include scale, so alt text need not.

questions.explanation: Alt text should include scale when relevant. Screen readers cannot infer size from dimensions.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use typography to distinguish primary from secondary fields
questions.stem: Derek's label uses identical typography for all fields; what typographic strategy would create hierarchy?

answer.exemplar: Using bold or larger type for the species name and lighter type for secondary fields would create clear hierarchy.

questions.explanation: Typographic variation creates hierarchy. Identical type flattens priority.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Avoid too many destinations on one sign
questions.stem: Ethan's wayfinding sign lists twenty destinations, overwhelming visitors who cannot find their target.

options.text: Visitors can scan twenty items quickly enough.
More destinations always help visitors find their way.
Limiting destinations per sign would reduce overload and speed scanning.
Colour coding alone fixes destination overload.

questions.explanation: Too many destinations overload visitors. Limiting per sign speeds scanning and decisions.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use clear error messages in navigation

stimulus.body: Fiona's tank app shows a cryptic error code when navigation fails, leaving users unable to recover.

questions.stem: What would improve Fiona's error handling?

options.text: Hiding errors entirely avoids user confusion.
Error codes are sufficient for all users.
Users should contact support instead of self-recovering.
Clear, actionable error messages would help users recover.

questions.explanation: Clear error messages enable recovery. Codes or hiding errors leave users stuck.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Use adequate line spacing for readability
questions.stem: George's tank log has cramped line spacing, making paragraphs hard to read and track.

options.text: Cramped spacing is fine because it saves vertical space.
Increasing line spacing would improve readability and tracking.
Readers can adjust spacing themselves in most viewers.
Line spacing does not affect reading comprehension.

questions.explanation: Cramped line spacing reduces readability. Adequate spacing aids tracking and comprehension.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Reserve white for clean backgrounds and avoid clutter

stimulus.body: Helen fills her tank log background with busy patterns, eliminating the clean white space that aids reading.

questions.stem: What problem does Helen's busy background create?

options.text: Readers can ignore backgrounds if they focus.
Patterns always improve visual interest enough to justify clutter.
Busy backgrounds reduce readability by removing clean white space.
White space is wasted space that should be filled.

questions.explanation: Busy backgrounds reduce readability. Clean white space aids focus and comprehension.
